clue.text: John Wall, who celebrated contemporary poets with glee

definitions.text: John Wall, who celebrated contemporary poets with glee

parts.words: John Wall, who celebrated contemporary poets with glee
parts.note: the clue gives the forenames of an English composer who set verse by poets of his day as glees, part-songs for unaccompanied voices

explanation.surface: A man called John Wall cheerfully praised the poets of his time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glee' reads as joy, but a glee is a short part-song for unaccompanied men's voices, popular in eighteenth-century England, and this composer wrote many of them.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wall Callcott (1766-1821) was an English composer best known for glees setting contemporary verse.

clue.text: Eliot's reference to Hadrian's soul?

parts.note: T. S. Eliot titled a poem after the Latin diminutive the emperor Hadrian used for his soul in his dying verses

explanation.surface: A question about where Eliot mentions the soul of the Roman emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Hadrian's deathbed poem begins 'Animula vagula blandula' ('little soul, wandering, gentle'); Eliot's 1929 Ariel poem takes its first word as its title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word means 'little soul', the emperor's own term, and it is also the title of Eliot's poem.

clue.text: Study of rights in speech

parts.note: the spoken word 'rights' is the same as 'rites', so this is the study of church rites

explanation.surface: An academic course on how people talk about their rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rights in speech' means a word that sounds like 'rights' when spoken: rites, the forms of public worship.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of liturgies, the formal rites of church worship, has this name.

clue.text: Dramatist makes a return in play, yes, a comedy

indicators.note: to make a return is to come back, so the letters found are read backwards
the letters sit inside the words play, yes, a comedy

explanation.surface: A playwright stages a comeback with a cheerful comic play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks YESACO, running across 'plaY, ES A COmedy'; 'makes a return' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean O'Casey was an Irish playwright, author of Juno and the Paycock.

clue.text: Second prize for 4' splay?

parts.note: read as 4's play, the clue names a play by the 4-down dramatist; a second prize is a silver cup, and a tassie is Scots for a cup

explanation.surface: An odd award given to something splayed four feet wide.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe has slipped: '4' splay' is 4's play, a play by the dramatist at 4-down. Second place wins silver; 'tassie' is a Scottish word for a cup, so a silver cup is the second prize.
explanation.definitionFit: O'Casey's 1928 anti-war play is titled after a Scots term for a silver drinking cup.

clue.text: Mistakes in Latin

parts.note: the Latin plural meaning 'things gone wrong', used for a printed list of corrections in a book

explanation.surface: Errors made in a Latin exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as errors in a schoolboy's Latin, but it asks for the Latin word for mistakes, still used for printing errors.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is Latin for errors and names a slip listing corrections to a printed book.

clue.text: Tom Sharpe's was not socially acceptable

definitions.text: Tom Sharpe's was not socially acceptable

parts.words: Tom Sharpe's was not socially acceptable
parts.note: Tom Sharpe's novel Indecent ___; 'not socially acceptable' stands for 'indecent', the missing first word of the title

explanation.surface: Something belonging to the novelist Tom Sharpe was improper.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Sharpe wrote the comic novel Indecent Exposure (1973); the clue's last words spell out 'indecent', leaving the second word as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The second word of the Sharpe title Indecent Exposure, a phrase for showing oneself in public.

clue.text: Jonah's father taking aim at it from a new angle

indicators.note: looking at the letters from a fresh angle means arranging them differently

explanation.surface: Jonah's father aims at something from a different direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from a new angle' rearranges the seven letters of AIM AT IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Jonah opens by naming the prophet as Jonah son of Amittai.

clue.text: Marine fossils from ancient kingdom of Jordan?

definitions.meaning: coiled shells of extinct sea creatures
the people of Ammon, whose capital Rabbah is now Amman in Jordan; the question mark admits that people stand for a kingdom

explanation.surface: Sea fossils dug up in the old lands of Jordan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both spiral-shelled fossil molluscs and the Biblical people of Ammon, east of the Jordan.

clue.text: They provided some emphasis traditionally, in the temple of Isis

definitions.text: They provided some emphasis traditionally, in the temple of Isis

indicators.note: only some of the letters of emphasis traditionally are taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Something gave the beat in the rites at an Egyptian goddess's temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks the run in 'emphaSIS TRAditionally'. The whole clue also describes them: these rattles marked the rhythm in Isis's worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sistrums, the plural here in Latin form, were metal rattles shaken in the cult of Isis.

clue.text: Deeply affected by Lyly

parts.note: describes a highly mannered prose style taken from John Lyly's Elizabethan romance Euphues

explanation.surface: Someone moved to the core by the writer Lyly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deeply affected' sounds like strong emotion, but it means very affected in style: the elaborate, artificial prose of Lyly's Euphues.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means an ornate, artificial literary style named after Lyly's hero Euphues.

clue.text: Luthier featured when Heifetz was on the fiddle

definitions.text: Luthier featured when Heifetz was on the fiddle

parts.words: Luthier featured when Heifetz was on the fiddle
parts.note: a violin-making family whose instrument Jascha Heifetz played, so the maker's name appeared whenever he performed

explanation.surface: A violin maker caught up when a great violinist was cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' suggests swindling, but it simply means playing the violin; Heifetz's favourite instrument was a Guarneri del Gesù of 1742.
explanation.definitionFit: The Guarneri family of Cremona made violins, and a luthier is a maker of stringed instruments.

clue.text: Austrian writer produces assorted tales with new ending

indicators.note: assorted things are mixed, so the letters of tales are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Austrian author turns out a mixed batch of stories, with a fresh conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assorted' rearranges TALES; 'with new ending' adds N (new) as the final letter, and 'produces' links the writer to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Felix Salten was the Austrian novelist who wrote Bambi.

clue.text: Sorceress could bring about a mail mix-up

indicators.note: a mix-up of the letters a mail means they are jumbled

explanation.surface: A witch could cause the post to go astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix-up' rearranges A MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth and Keats's poem, Lamia is an enchantress, a serpent in a woman's form.

clue.text: Duty of reading post in church

definitions.text: Duty of reading post in church

parts.words: Duty of reading post in church
parts.note: the office of a lector, the person who reads the lessons in church

explanation.surface: Someone's task is opening the letters in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reading post' suggests going through the mail, but 'post' is a job: the office of reader in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectorate is the office of lector, a cleric or layperson appointed to read scripture in services.

clue.text: Run off too many, though by definition a superior picture

definitions.meaning: to print more copies than needed
taken literally, an image that is above, over another print

explanation.surface: Printing too many copies, though strictly the result is a better image.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means printing excess copies, and also printing something on top of an existing image, as on stamps.

clue.text: Payments made for palace neckwear?

parts.note: palace means royal, as in a royal residence
ties are worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Money spent on cravats for the palace staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made for' links the payments to the neckwear that builds them.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalties are sums paid to an author or rights holder for each copy sold.

clue.text: Die aware, perhaps, and tired as a lady richly left

definitions.text: tired as a lady richly left

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of die aware might form something else

explanation.surface: Die knowingly, and weary like a wealthy heiress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges DIE AWARE. 'A lady richly left' is Portia in The Merchant of Venice, who says her little body is aweary of the great world.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word means wearied or tired, used in Shakespeare for Portia's weariness.

clue.text: Surely never heard between setter and solver?

definitions.text: Surely never heard between setter and solver?

parts.words: Surely never heard between setter and solver?
parts.note: an angry word, a ..., should never pass between the one who sets a puzzle and the one who does it

explanation.surface: A remark that puzzle setters and solvers would never exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle that passes between them is itself the answer, and also, split in two, an angry word that is never spoken between friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it means an angry remark; as one word it is the puzzle linking setter and solver.

clue.text: Partridge's provenance

definitions.meaning: Eric Partridge wrote an etymological dictionary of English with this title
where things come from, their sources

explanation.surface: Where the partridge comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Partridge's 1958 dictionary of word sources bears this title, and the word means sources or beginnings.

clue.text: We hear melodies from eccentric poet

indicators.note: we hear signals a word spoken that sounds like the one to write

parts.note: airs are tunes or melodies

explanation.surface: Tunes are heard from an odd poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' says AIRS, tunes. Pam Ayres is an English poet famous for comic, quirky verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Pam Ayres is a popular English writer of humorous, offbeat verse, hence an eccentric poet.

clue.text: Choose artist for Greek tragedy

parts.note: to elect is to choose
RA, Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: Pick an artist for a Greek tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is the title of tragedies by both Sophocles and Euripides.

clue.text: "I… made them -s / Of mine own moods" (Francis Thompson, Poems, 1893)

definitions.text: "I… made them -s / Of mine own moods" (Francis Thompson, Poems, 1893)

parts.words: "I… made them -s / Of mine own moods" (Francis Thompson, Poems, 1893)
parts.note: a quotation with one word missing, to be filled from Thompson's poem; the -s shows the missing word is a plural noun given here in the singular

explanation.surface: A line of verse by Francis Thompson with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash stands for the missing word; '-s' means the poem has its plural, and the grid takes the singular.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gives form to something, as the poet says he made others mould his own moods.

clue.text: Wycherley character attached to manly page

definitions.text: Wycherley character attached to manly page

parts.words: Wycherley character attached to manly page
parts.note: in Wycherley's comedy The Plain Dealer, the hero is named Manly and this woman is his fickle beloved, who becomes attached to his page

explanation.surface: A character from a Restoration play who is fond of a strapping young servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manly' looks like an adjective, but Manly is the hero of The Plain Dealer; the woman he loves falls for his page, Fidelia, a girl disguised as a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivia is Manly's faithless mistress in William Wycherley's The Plain Dealer (1676).

clue.text: He grew dainty of his worth, Ulysses thought

definitions.text: He grew dainty of his worth, Ulysses thought

parts.words: He grew dainty of his worth, Ulysses thought
parts.note: in Troilus and Cressida Ulysses says of the sulking Greek champion that he grows dainty of his worth

explanation.surface: A man became fussy about his own value, in Ulysses's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida, Ulysses complains that the great warrior, sulking in his tent, 'Grows dainty of his worth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proud Greek hero of the Trojan War is the subject of Ulysses's complaint in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: For whose party did Leighphiles vote?

definitions.text: For whose party did Leighphiles vote?

parts.words: For whose party did Leighphiles vote?
parts.note: Leighphiles are fans of the playwright Mike Leigh, whose best-known play names a woman's party; the vote suggests a political party

explanation.surface: Which political party did a group of supporters back?
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political, but it is Mike Leigh's 1977 play Abigail's Party; the grid gives the possessive without its apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail's Party is Mike Leigh's comedy about a suburban drinks gathering, so fans of Leigh would favour that party.

clue.text: "Look to the widow, she —— white" (Thomas Middleton, The Plain Dealer)

definitions.text: "Look to the widow, she —— white" (Thomas Middleton, The Plain Dealer)

parts.words: "Look to the widow, she —— white" (Thomas Middleton, The Plain Dealer)
parts.note: a quotation with a verb missing, saying what the widow does with white make-up

explanation.surface: A line from an old play about watching a widow.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash marks the missing verb: the widow uses white cosmetic. The Plain Dealer is in fact Wycherley's play, as at 22-across.
explanation.definitionFit: To put make-up on one's face, here white lead to look young, is to apply cosmetics with a brush.

clue.text: What Twenty Years After inevitably did

definitions.text: What Twenty Years After inevitably did

parts.words: What Twenty Years After inevitably did
parts.note: Dumas's novel Twenty Years After is the sequel to The Three Musketeers, so it followed on from it, as twenty years always come after

explanation.surface: What happened when two decades had passed.
explanation.walkthrough: Twenty Years After is Alexandre Dumas's sequel to The Three Musketeers: a sequel necessarily follows its original, and so does any later period.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a result or in sequence, as a sequel follows the first book.

clue.text: Bronte family to merit Irish playwright

parts.note: to merit something is to earn it
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish dramatist

explanation.surface: A family in Bronte's fiction deserves an Irish dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earnshaws are the family of Catherine and Hindley in Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights.
